Join OpenAI, AWS, JPM, Troutman Pepper, Pear VC, NEA, and Cathay Innovation for a one-day healthcare AI hackathon bringing together engineers, clinicians, researchers, designers, and founders to build products that solve real problems across health.
Why Attend?
🏆 Compete for up to $5,000 in first/second/third place cash prizes, advisory meetings with leading healthcare AI operators and industry sponsors, and 1:1 pitch opportunities with PearX, NEA, and Cathay

🚀 Connect with leaders from OpenAI, AWS, Stanford Medicine, J.P. Morgan, and leading VC-backed healthcare startups

Presented by Pear VC · NEA · Cathay Innovation
Powered by OpenAI · AWS · J.P. Morgan · Troutman Pepper
Healthcare is the largest industry in the world, yet much of its infrastructure still runs on fragmented software, manual workflows, and administrative overhead. Recent advances in foundation models and AI agents have created an opportunity to rethink how healthcare is delivered, from the clinician desktop to the insurance back office to the patient experience.
Life sciences is entering a similar inflection point, as advances in foundation models, biological data, and increasingly automated experimentation begin to reshape how we understand and engineer biology. From target discovery and molecular design to clinical development, AI is creating new ways to compress the traditional drug development cycle and build entirely new categories of therapeutics and research tools.
Throughout the day you'll work directly with venture investors, startup founders, physicians, and operators who spend every day building healthcare companies.
Teams will leave with relationships, recruiting opportunities, and potentially the foundation for their next startup.
Whether you're already building in healthcare or just discovering the space, you'll spend the day working on problems that matter.
What Should You Build?
Build something that meaningfully improves health.
We're less interested in incremental AI wrappers and more interested in products that unlock new capabilities, create new business models, or solve long-standing problems across the healthcare and life sciences ecosystem.
Some areas we're especially excited about include:
🧬 Care Delivery & Clinical Innovation
Build AI that makes care more accessible, personalized, and effective , from diagnostics and specialty care to home-based care, clinical trials, robotics, and entirely new models of care delivery.

🏥 Healthcare Infrastructure & Financing
Build AI that fixes the systems behind healthcare , improving how care is financed, administered, coordinated, and delivered across providers, payers, employers, marketplaces, and supply chains.

🔬 AI × Life Sciences
Build AI that better predicts what will actually happen in biology , using richer, multi-compartment data to model real-world outcomes such as toxicity, delivery, efficacy, and clinical trial endpoints rather than focusing only on molecular binding.

These are examples, not constraints. If you have a compelling idea that improves healthcare, feel free to build it because we want to see it!

Join us for Battle of the Personal Brains , a 5 hour hands-on AI hackathon where you’ll build an intelligent personal agent powered by your own data, live information, and create an agentic workflow to take action, all under one roof at the Bright Data office in SOMA.
Build the personal AI agent you’ve always wanted.
In today’s world, it’s possible for an AI agent to know what you know - your emails, your documents, meetings, calendar, tasks, files, and other information that’s relevant to you - and then act on it.
For this hackathon, the challenge is simple: Build a brain. Build an agent. Then make it do something.
🗓️ Event Details
When: 4:00 PM – 9:00 PM, Monday September 21, 2026

Where: Bright Data office, San Francisco, CA

🧠 First, Build your Personal Brain
Your agent is only as useful as the information it can understand. So you’ll create an AI-powered brain that can combine knowledge from multiple sources:
Your laptop and local files

Google Drive and cloud documents

Personal email and other data sources

Public information from across the web

Meeting notes, receipts, photos, schedules, and more

You'll use Cognee ’s structured AI memory to create your Personal Brain , and Bright Data to discover and retrieve public web data.
🤖 Then, Build your Agent
Once your agent can access the right knowledge, the real fun begins. Build an agent that can find information, reason across it, and take action.
Your agent could:
Manage your calendar - Find availability and schedule an appointment automatically.

Take notes and remind you later - Capture information and send a reminder exactly when you need it.

Turn meetings into action - Read meeting summaries, identify commitments and action items, and build your personal to-do schedule.

Handle your expenses - Process receipts, extract the important information, organize them, and prepare expense reports.

Organize and share your photos - Process photos, upload them to Google Photos, organize them, and share them with your WhatsApp group.

Build your own personal assistant - Create an agent that understands your information, remembers what's important, and helps you get things done.

Connect your digital life - Connect to apps and services you use every day, read through information, create notes, identify what matters, and remind you when action is required.

Or build something completely different.
Your brain. Your agent. Your idea.

Data + Memory + Reasoning + Tools + Actions

This isn't just about building another chatbot. We're looking for agents that can understand information and then accomplish something useful.

About Event

WHAT IS re:AGENT

re:AGENT is a two-day build weekend focused on the infrastructure scientific agents still need: better datasets, sharper tools, and reliable ways to evaluate their work. Participants will use Paperclip , Proto , Claude , and other scientific AI tools to build systems that can take on real scientific problems and produce results worth trusting.
Paperclip turns papers, datasets, clinical trials, and biological databases into an agent-native workspace that AI systems can search, synthesize, and build upon. Proto is a design framework and infrastructure layer for generative biology, allowing builders to combine AI models and search for DNA, RNA, or protein sequences that satisfy custom criteria.
The weekend brings together engineers, scientists, computational biologists, founders, and AI researchers. Projects might include assembling a research-ready dataset that would be impractical to create by hand, along with the analysis needed to show that its findings are real. Others might involve designing a new biological system to a defined specification and testing whether it holds up against existing evidence.
The aim is not just to accelerate existing workflows, but to create the tools, datasets, and evaluation methods that make entirely new scientific questions and experiments possible.
READY TO BUILD?

If you're excited about the future of AI, agents and scientific discovery, we'll see you there...
We will close applications on Thursday, 30th of July, 12 PM PST. Spots will be confirmed on Friday, 31st of July.

People with the questions: scientists of all stripes. Wet lab, computational, clinical, industry. Biology, biochemistry, biophysics, chemistry, structural. Anyone with a real problem, ideally a real dataset, and the judgment to tell right from wrong results.
People who build for a living: ML engineers, software developers, and agent builders who can take a half-formed scientific problem and ship something that runs by Sunday.
No prior AI expertise required. Participants are welcome at all levels.

Tracks
Track A: Build an AI Scientist
Build an AI agent that can carry out a defined scientific or drug-development workflow from start to finish. It should gather evidence, use relevant tools or databases, generate and test hypotheses, produce a structured output, and make its reasoning easy to inspect. This could mean reasoning over experimental data, scientific literature, or learned representations like protein embeddings. Examples include a virtual FDA reviewer, toxicology agent, clinical trial designer, experimental planning agent, or a protein-discovery agent that generates and tests hypotheses over protein embeddings and structural features.
Track B: Build a Dataset or Meta-Analysis

What have you always wanted the literature to tell you, but could never read fast enough to find out? Draft the queries, run them across thousands of papers, sharpen and re-run until the results hold the specific pieces you care about. Following the first edition in Rome, which brought together 70+ participants, including Italian Navy engineers, and produced five working prototypes, the challenge now crosses the Atlantic to the Bay Area’s deep-tech ecosystem.
Over 48 hours, engineers, developers, founders, researchers and designers will form teams to build working solutions around real maritime and defense engineering challenges , with access to technical mentors, development hardware and potential opportunities to continue developing the strongest concepts beyond the event.

OT Cybersecurity & Blast Radius Analysis

Piping Layout Optimization

Software-Defined Vessel

Build with Real Hardware
Participants will have access to a selection of Qualcomm and Arduino technologies during the hackathon, including Snapdragon-powered laptops, edge AI and robotics development platforms, Arduino prototyping hardware and supporting developer tools.
These tools are intended for hands-on technical development . Participants with experience in areas such as software development, embedded systems, electronics, robotics, edge AI, computer vision or hardware prototyping will be best positioned to take full advantage of them.
Qualcomm and Arduino technologies will be introduced during the opening session so teams can quickly understand the available resources and integrate hardware, edge AI, computer vision, sensors or robotics into their prototypes.
Exact hardware configurations will be shared with participants ahead of the event.
More Than a 48-Hour Hackathon
The goal is not only to build a prototype, but to identify ideas with the potential to continue developing after the event.
Work on real Fincantieri challenges with potential relevance to future maritime and defense applications.

Compete for a Qualcomm-powered laptop awarded to the winning team.

Develop your concept beyond the hackathon: selected promising prototypes may have the opportunity to continue evolving.

Access Fincantieri expertise: winning and particularly promising concepts may receive mentoring from Fincantieri’s network of experts to help further mature the solution and explore its potential application within Fincantieri.

Connect with leading technical talent from industry, academia, venture capital and the defense innovation ecosystem.

Partners & Ecosystem
The hackathon is powered by Fincantieri , Mind The Bridge and Silicon Mountain .
Qualcomm is the main technology sponsor, supporting participants with hardware, development resources and technology expertise throughout the event.
Additional experts from Fincantieri, academia, industry, venture capital and the defense innovation ecosystem will support teams through mentoring and judging.

48 hours of hands-on building and prototyping

Real technical challenges provided by Fincantieri

Access to Qualcomm and Arduino hardware and development resources

Mentors and domain experts supporting teams throughout the event

Collaboration with engineers, founders, and researchers

A Qualcomm-powered laptop prize for the winning team

Potential follow-on development opportunities for the most promising concepts

The Collaborative Agent Hackathon is a one-day event for building open-source, collaborative AI agents using Flower.
Agents are changing what is possible, and their greatest potential emerges when they collaborate safely in human-supervised multi-agent teams.
Participants will form teams on the day, develop a working prototype and present it at the end of the event. Each team will explore how open-source collaborative agents of varying complexity can work together safely.

Build an open-source agent or multi-agent system using Flower in which the safe collaboration of agent teams is central to the solution.

Automate a task

Form self-improving loops with one another

Operate across distributed machines and datasets

It gets built by communities — developers leveling up together, founders stress-testing ideas with peers, researchers colliding with practitioners in the same room. In September 2025, we opened our space in the heart of Silicon Valley. Not for vendor pitches. Not for product demos. For the conversations and connections that actually move the field forward.

About Event

Build It. Test It. Prove It.
Smells like a hackathon. Runs like a pressure test, on you, not just your idea.
Proving Ground runs a three-day Sprint where judges push past the pitch. No script survives real questions about what you tried, what broke, and what you changed.
Past teams have gone on to raise from 500 Global and Blitzscaling Ventures, and been accepted into Berkeley SkyDeck and Confluent's accelerator, independently, without Proving Ground's involvement in those decisions.
What this is
A hackathon judges what you built by the end. We watch during the process and look past the end to what may come next.

The team is almost everything. How you make decisions under pressure, how you handle a setback, how you treat each other when something breaks. You'll document that as you go. What we ask you to show and how we question it are built around behavior, not performance.
How it works
Over three days, founders build under real constraint. No script, no rehearsed demo. Judges probe what you tried, what broke, and what you changed, and compare where you started to where you ended.
Two Tracks
Discovery Track. Pre-market, no active customer contact yet. For the startup curious, including enterprise folks seriously exploring a leap.
Pre-seed Track. In-market, already talking to customers. Ship something real, show what's changed, pressure-test your next move.
After the Sprint
Select teams get invited into the Street Test: 30 days back in the real world, no artificial deadline, no audience. This is where we see if momentum was real or borrowed from the room. It's the part a hackathon can't offer, because a hackathon ends when the weekend does.

candidates.title: 💎GemJam: Use AI to Make & 3D Print Jewelry in One Night!
candidates.evidence:
💎GemJam: Use AI to Make & 3D Print Jewelry in One Night!
Ever wanted to design your own jewelry and actually wear it that night?
Machine Cinema brings you a whole new GenJam concept: A GemJam! We've never done this before. A hackathon where we use AI to design 2D jewelry concepts, use AI to turn them into 3D objects, use 3D printers to print them, use AI to create video commercials for the jewelry, and then see it modeled on the runway, that night!
2D Design your jewelry...💎
Turn that into a 3D Design...💍
3D Print it...🖨️
Turn that into an AI Commercial...🎞️
and then see it on the Runway! 🕺
Don't get it yet? Here's a video of how it works. And yes, we're crazy, but at Machine Cinema, we always want to try crazier and crazier maker event ideas. And don’t worry, the tools are easy to use! We’ll walk you through everything end to end.
FREE FOOD & DRINK PROVIDED!
Massive thank you to our partners Martini.film and Hyper3D for supporting us on this experiment!

That is the whole idea. You sketch a piece, design it with AI, we print it in the room, you make a commercial for it, and you walk out with it on.
The printer takes about 50 minutes, so you make the AI ad while it runs. By the end of the night you have a real object and a commercial!
We know, it's a crazy idea, but in a world of vibe coding hackathons, Threejs websites, and yet another panel/fireside chat, we thought let's push things as far as we can go. Why not?
(Also, if you don't want to jam but you just want to see what people made, no problem! Just come for the runway show and catch all the creations.)
Ticket prices go to funding the 3D printing, dinner, and drinks. Bring your fanciest clothing and dress up and join us!

🛠️ Part One: The GenJam
2pm to 6pm. You build.
🎨 Concept. Generate your design with image tools.
🧊 Model. Turn it into a printable mesh with Hyper3D. Free credits!
🖨️ Print. Send the file to Itemfarm. 50 minutes on the bed.
🎬 Ad. Cut a commercial with Martini.film while you wait. Free credits for everyone.
Feel free to bring your own team or come solo and we'll match you with new friends.

✨ Part Two: The Runway
6pm to 8pm. Come to see the jewelry modeled on the runway! Dress up if you want, and if you want to model, let us know in registration.
📸 Step and repeat at the door.
👠 Your piece walks. Your ad plays behind it.
🗳️ Everyone votes on their favorites. Product and commercial, judged together.
🏅 Winner gets their jewelry cast in bronze.
Drinks and finger food. Come for the runway even if you missed the jam.

👥 Who it's for
AI creators, jewelry and product designers, 3D artists, fashion-tech builders, marketers. No 3D experience needed.
🎁 What you leave with
A piece of jewelry. A commercial. New friends. And a thrilling night.
🤝 Partners
Martini.film is an amazing collaborative AI video tool that allows you to work collaboratively in teams to co-create AI video. We'll use it for the AI commercial, with free credits for every participant.

Hyper3D is a great tool for turning any 2D object into a printable 3D object. And it can do it in less than 3 minutes!
Generate & Refine with Hyper3D Rodin
Turn a 2D concept into a high-detail, controllable, print-ready 3D model with Hyper3D Rodin.
Rodin goes beyond one-shot 3D generation, giving creators precise control over geometry, part structure, local details, and multi-color output — making it especially well suited for jewelry and physical fabrication.
Why Rodin for 3D Printing
Powerful Part-Level Control
Automatically or manually split a model into clean structural parts, continue splitting individual parts as needed, and refine or enhance local details with smooth, structure-aware boundaries.
3D ControlNet Geometry Guidance
Use reference geometry to control shape, proportions, and silhouette more precisely.
10M+ Ultra-Detailed Geometry
Preserve fine sculptural details, engravings, surface textures, and intricate jewelry features directly in the mesh.
Multi-Color 3MF Workflow
Export 3MF with colors automatically mapped to different parts for easier multi-color 3D printing.
Print-Ready Geometry & Formats
Support for watertight geometry and common fabrication formats, helping models move into slicing and printing workflows with less cleanup.
From AI concept to physical object — with far more control over what actually gets printed.

Itemfarm has amazing 3D Printers that can print multiple objects at the same time, allowing us to print jewelry for everyone in attendance!

Seats are limited. RSVP early.

This GemJam is part of a new GenJam Fashion Series that Machine Cinema is working on. Let us know if you'd like to support or help with the next one.

candidates.evidence:
The Next Interface Hackathon: Rethink how we talk to AI
For three years, using AI meant typing into a box and waiting for text to come back.
That era is ending. 

The next interface isn't a chat window. It's worn, spoken, and always on.
Glasses that listen.
A pendant that remembers. 
A tracker you never charge. 
A second self that watches your screen and acts before you ask.
We're putting the founders building that future in one room with the people who want to build on it.

Half a day in San Francisco. 

Real hardware on the table. Working demos, not slideware.
The lineup is a short list of founders shipping the wearables that are pulling AI off the screen. 

The founders in the room:
Adam Cohen Hillel, Secondly - a personal AI "second self" that sees your screen and acts across every app you use. The chat box becomes a presence.
Nik Shevchenko, Omi - the open-source AI wearable necklace, with 250+ developer apps already built on it. Always listening, always yours.
AnhPhu Nguyen, Mira - AI smart glasses with no camera. They hear what you hear, recall every name, and translate 60+ languages in under a second. AnhPhu is the Harvard builder behind last year's viral I-XRAY demo.
Andy Kong, Chargerless - a 7-gram health tracker powered by daylight. One minute of sun a day and it never needs a charger.
What you'll build: pick a device, an API, or a live sensor stream. 

Ship something a person could actually wear or talk to by the time we demo.

 The strongest builds demo to the founders in the room.
This is for builders, hardware hackers, AI engineers, and designers who think the keyboard is a temporary technology.

About Event

Car AI Navigation Hackathon

Challenge: We have a mini city road with lanes, intersection and traffic signs. Your job is to use AI and a small autonomous car like the Donkeycar or equivalent (typically 1/16th scale or smaller RC car with a Raspberry Pi or equivalent and a camera controlling it) to navigate the "city", obeying signs and making it from one side to the other in the fastest time.

You must bring your own car, which should be ready to run, with compute and camera already onboard and working. The objective of the hackathon is to add AI "city" navigation to it.

You can use onboard AI, AI on your laptop via Wifi or AI in the cloud to help with the navigation. Think creatively about what kind of AI to use and what's the fastest way to do it!

This is not an event for spectators, nor will cars be provided to those who arrive without one. This is a hackathon, not a regular race. Come ready to hack!
